title: Compliance Note on Statute-of-Limitations Expiry in Two-Payment Settlement Offers
content:
# Two-Payment Settlement — Statute-of-Limitations Reductions

The statute-of-limitations expiry date that a Placed Consumer Accounts record carries bears on the price of a Two-Payment Settlement offer under Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements.

**Rule.** Where the account's statute-of-limitations expiry date is before the offer date, the Two-Payment time-barred reduction of 5.0 points applies; where that expiry date is on the offer date or within the 180 calendar days after it, the Two-Payment near-expiry reduction of 2.0 points applies; a later expiry date carries no statute reduction.

## Input — judgement — output

| Expiry date on the placed account, against the offer date | Judgement | Reduction |
|---|---|---|
| before the offer date | time-barred | 5.0 percentage points |
| on the offer date, or 1 to 180 calendar days after it | near expiry | 2.0 percentage points |
| 181 or more calendar days after the offer date | neither | none |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Expiry date the day before the offer date: 5.0 points.
- Expiry date on the offer date itself: 2.0 points, not 5.0 — the time-barred band needs an expiry date strictly before the offer date.
- Expiry date the 180th calendar day after the offer date: 2.0 points.
- Expiry date the 181st calendar day after the offer date: no statute reduction.
